newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil, Venezuela sign energy, road agreements.
newsitem.headline: Brazil, Venezuela sign energy, road agreements.

text.p: Brazil and Venezuela on Friday signed agreements to integrate their electricity distribution networks and finance cross-border highways through the Amazon, officials said.
Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso and his Venezuelan counterpart Rafael Caldera met for a one-day summit in the city of Boa Vista in Brazil's northernmost state of Roraima.

"I have always said South American integration cannot be limited to commerce. It is based on a tripod made up of free trade, energy integration and physical interconnection," Cardoso said according to a speech text issued by his office.
The first agreement involved completing a cross-border transmission line so Venezuela's Electrificacion del Caroni (Edelca) can supply Roraima with much-needed energy.
Venezuelan diplomatic sources in Brasilia said the line was expected to cost some $500 million.

The second accord allows for $86 million in Andean Development Corporation (CAF) financing to pave a road from Boa Vista to the frontier, thus linking the Venezuelan capital Caracas and Manaus, capital of Brazil's Amazonas state.
The highway would finally join the Amazon to the Caribbean and open up a route to North America, Cardoso said.
After signing the agreements in Boa Vista, Cardoso and Caldera were due to fly to Manaus where they were scheduled to attemd a meeting of Venezuelan and Brazilian businessmen.
After a period of neglect, with Venezuela looking north to the United States and Brazil south to the Mercosur common market, the two countries have recently started to intensify their relations.
Venezuelan officials say oil-rich Caracas considers itself the natural energy provider to the rest of the continent, especially South America's industrial powerhouse Brazil.

Venezuela's state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela SA (PdVSA) and Brazil's Petrobras have been discussing possible joint ventures, including the purchase in the Caribbean or the construction in Brazil of an oil refinery, diplomats said.
